newsitem.title: CROATIA: Domestic, export demand seen key to Croatia growth.
newsitem.headline: Domestic, export demand seen key to Croatia growth.

text.p: Croatia's economic recovery will hinge on a further rise in domestic consumption and investment in 1997, but it may be slowed by uncertain export demand, the leading Zagrebacka Banka said on Thursday.

"The upward trend of GDP (gross domestic product) will depend primarily upon further invigorating domestic consumption and investments," chief economist Zarko Miljenovic said in his latest quarterly forecast.

But he said the dynamics of export growth remain clouded by weak recovery in demand from Western markets. The ability of Croatian products to win new markets and expand in central and eastern Europe is also questionable.
Miljenovic lowered his estimate for the 1997 growth rate to 5.5 percent from 6.3 percent.
He also revised down last year's GDP rise to 4.1 from 4.8 percent due to "slower than expected" third quarter growth.
Lower export demand and higher industry labour costs caused industrial output, which represents one third of GDP, to slump in September. It only picked up in October, he said.

"Despite dynamic growth in personal consumption and tourism, the absence of an increase in the export of goods...as well as a decrease in public consumption, resulted in slower growth of GDP," Miljenovic said.
Helped by performance in tourism, Croatia's key trade and currency earner, the economy was seen as expanding 9.0 percent in the third quarter of 1996 and a further 1.0 percent in the fourth.

Miljenovic said he had raised his overall 1995 growth estimate to 1.7 percent from 1.5 percent after including higher final employment figures in the small business sector -- a growing segment of the economy. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
